title: What broke when I used AI to build a clay-style Android roguelite
author: Remedion
selftext:
I've been building Clay Hero, a top-down action roguelite for Android with a handmade plasticine look. I use generative AI for much of the production work, and I direct the game and play-test changes on my phone. I wanted to share what the pipeline looks like, what broke, and how other devs handle the same problems.



\*\*The pipeline\*\*



\- Characters, bosses, and level props start as image-to-3D models. The raw models looked like they came from different games, so I repaint them using camera projection and a shared clay palette. I use reference images to guide the painted eyes.

\- For the characters in this pipeline, I use a shared 17-bone rig in Blender. Scripts generate the basic movement and combat clips plus about 11 ability animations. I adjust the idle poses for different body types, especially bipeds and quadrupeds.

\- For sound effects, I generate several takes in ElevenLabs and pick the one that fits the action.

\- Claude Code and Codex wrote most of the Unity code and the Blender and Unity tooling. I decide what gets built and use phone play-tests to judge whether it actually feels right.



\*\*What went wrong\*\*



\- \*\*A good model can still look out of place.\*\* Getting the colors and surfaces to feel like they belong to the same game mattered more than making each model look impressive on its own.

\- \*\*A batch re-export dropped the ability clips.\*\* A before-and-after comparison caught it. I now render a comparison for each batch so I can spot missing clips and broken poses.

\- \*\*Still images only tell me so much.\*\* They help catch floating feet and awkward poses. Playing on a small phone screen is where I find out whether I can read an incoming attack and react in time.



\*\*What I'm curious about\*\*



How do you keep generated models consistent across a whole game? For animation, do you script your own clips, retarget existing sets, or use a mix?



If you use AI coding assistants, I'd also love to hear which decisions you keep hands-on and what checks have saved you from regressions.



I haven't opened the closed Google Play test yet. If you'd like to test Clay Hero on Android, you can sign up at https://remediongames.com/#test. I'll send Google Play invitations once the test opens and spots are available. Real-money purchases will be enabled in the test.
